title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported deaths of at least 9 people and 39 others in a critical condition after consuming spurious Indian-Made Foreign Liquor in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat
subtitle:
The Commission issues notices to the Gujarat Chief Secretary and Director General of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report to include updated status of the death toll, hospitalised victims, investigation, departmental action initiated against erring officers, relief, compensation and medical assistance provided to the families of the deceased and to the survivors
Information also sought on long-term measures to prevent such tragedies
body_text:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of media reports that at least 9 people died and 39 others were hospitalised in a critical condition after consuming spurious Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat. Reportedly, the illicit liquor was spiked with a high concentration of methanol and was being sold in counterfeit bottles bearing the label of a popular brand. The illicit liquor racket came to light during an investigation of an accidental death case registered for the death of a police recruit.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Gujarat Chief Secretary and Director General of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
The report is expected to include the updated status of the death toll, hospitalised victims and investigation including the steps taken to trace the entire supply chain of methanol and other raw materials. It should also include the details of the departmental action initiated against the suspended police personnel and any other erring officials, relief, compensation and medical assistance provided to the families of the deceased and to the survivors. Besides, the Commission has also sought a report on the long-term measures being implemented to strengthen the enforcement of the prohibition law and prevent such tragedies.
According to the media reports, a large manufacturing setup was uncovered and chemicals, colouring agents, ready-filled counterfeit liquor bottles, fake branded stickers and sticker rolls, bottle caps and cardboard packaging material were seized by police.
***
NSK

enrichment.summary: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has taken suo motu cognizance of reports that at least 9 people died and 39 others were hospitalised after consuming spurious liquor spiked with methanol in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat. The counterfeit liquor was sold in bottles mimicking a popular IMFL brand, and the racket surfaced during investigation of a police recruit's death. NHRC has issued notices to Gujarat's Chief Secretary and DGP seeking a detailed report within two weeks covering the death toll, investigation status, action against erring officials including suspended police personnel, compensation to victims, and long-term measures to strengthen prohibition enforcement.
enrichment.context:
Gujarat has enforced prohibition since 1960 under the Bombay Prohibition Act, making it one of the few 'dry' states in India alongside Bihar and a few others. Despite the ban, spurious liquor tragedies have recurred periodically in the state, often linked to illicit manufacturing networks that adulterate liquor with industrial methanol, which is toxic and can cause blindness or death even in small quantities. Such incidents typically expose gaps in enforcement, alleged police complicity, and weak supply-chain regulation of chemicals used in counterfeit liquor production.

The NHRC, a statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, has the power to take suo motu cognizance of human rights violations, including deaths caused by state negligence or failure to enforce the law, and can call for reports from state authorities. This intervention is part of the Commission's broader mandate to hold state machinery accountable for lapses that result in loss of life, particularly where law enforcement or regulatory failure is implicated, as in the alleged involvement of police personnel in this case.

prelims_questions.question:
With reference to the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India, consider the following statements:
1. It was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
2. It can take suo motu cognizance of human rights violations reported in the media.
3. Its recommendations are legally binding on state governments.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: NHRC was established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 and can take suo motu cognizance of rights violations based on media reports, as seen in this case. However, its recommendations are advisory in nature and not legally binding on governments.
